security_spec.violation_condition: In the Linux kernel, when a context switch or VM-entry/VM-exit saves and restores xivt (sivt/mivt/hivt) without also saving and restoring the xivt.EHV bit, or when the kernel assumes synchronous exceptions always trap via xtvec while xivt.EHV is set, the kernel's trap handler entry logic is bypassed or corrupted.
security_spec.summary: xivt.EHV bit silently redirects synchronous exceptions (ECALLs, page faults, illegal instructions) through the xivt-based vector table instead of xtvec; kernel context switch and KVM must atomically save/restore xivt.EHV alongside xivt to prevent a guest or userspace task from hijacking the kernel's trap entry path.

findings.finding: CSR_SIVT (0x107), CSR_MIVT (0x307), CSR_HIVT (0x607) macros are not defined. The Smaivt/Ssmaivt/smehv extensions are not yet implemented in this kernel. No EHV bit definitions exist for xIVT CSRs.

Context switch saves ra/sp/s0-s11, sstatus.SUM, and shadow stack pointer only. No xIVT CSR save/restore because the extension is unsupported. If smehv were enabled, this would be a privilege-escalation bug because xIVT.EHV would leak across tasks.
switch_to() macro saves FPU, vector, and CSR_ENVCFG. No xIVT handling. With smehv, this macro must also swap xIVT CSR state and the EHV bit.

KVM VM-entry/exit swaps SSTATUS/STVEC/SEPC/SSCRATCH between host and guest. No xIVT CSR handling. With smehv, a guest that programs xIVT.EHV could trigger host trap handlers via the guest-controlled vector table.

kvm_arch_vcpu_load writes VSSTATUS/VSIE/VSTVEC/VSSCRATCH/VSEPC/VSCAUSE/VSTVAL/HVIP/VSATP/HENVCFG/HSTATEEN0. No xIVT CSR written. With smehv, guest xIVT values and EHV bit would not be properly virtualized.

kvm_vcpu_csr struct lacks vsivt/vmivt/vhivt fields and any EHV bit tracking. kvm_vcpu_arch lacks host_sivt/host_mivt/host_hivt shadow fields. These are required for proper KVM virtualization of smehv-capable guests.

Signal frame saves FPU, vector, and CFI/Zicfiss extension state only. No xIVT/EHV extension state entry. Without smehv signal support, a task's xIVT register state (including EHV) would be lost across signal delivery and sigreturn.
No RISCV_ISA_EXT_SMEHV or RISCV_ISA_EXT_SSEHV defined among the 128 extension slots (currently using up to 105/127). The kernel has no mechanism to detect or advertise smehv/ssehv hardware support.
